full_judgment:
3. Mr. B. N. Chowdhury, learned Counsel appearing for the appellant has submitted that another decision of a Single Judge of the Leigh Court in the case of Sultan Ahmed Vs. Hazera Khatoon (C.Rev. Case Nos. 130 and 131 of 1969) which has dissented from the view taken in the case of Abdul Hamid and has held that on and from 14th April, 1956 the relationship of landlord and tenant ceased with the acquisition of rent receiving interest under the Act. Thus with the severance of landlord and tenant relation, the decree-holder ceased to have his right to put the holding to sale under the Bengal Tenancy Act. But his right to proceed against the judgment-debtor remained unaffected and the decree-holder retained his right, title and interest of the judgment-debtor in the property to that extent. The landlord could realize the amount by a suit, which of course wills in substance he a money suit. The view expressed by Sen., J. in this decision, we find, is in accord with law. 

 4. Details of the history as the right to the rent of the extent receiver on the acquisition of the rent receiving interest need not be set out in detail, excepting that when the rent suit was filed in 1960 the law as to right of extent receiver to recover arrear rent is to be found in section 63C of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act which, inter alia, provides that all arrears of rent and cuss together with interest thereon which remained due to any rent receiver in respect of any interest on the date of acquisition, and which have not become barred by limitation shall continue to be recoverable by such rent receiver amicably or through Civil Court, from the persons liable to pay them. We have referred only to the re event part bereft of irrelevant parts. This provision of law no doubt has preserved the right of extent receiver to realize his dues as rent from his ex-tenants and this right is therefore to be construed in the light of the other provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Under section 3 of the Act, with the notification made in the Official Gazette all rent receiving interests of the rent receiver shall vest absolutely in the Government free from all encumbrances. It is not disputed that on and from 14th April, 1956 rent receiving interest of all rent receivers in Bangladesh were acquired under this section, and so the relationship of landlord and tenant so far as the previous rent receivers are concerned ceased to exist. The suit could be filed as money suit and the decree holder in any suit whether described as money suit or rent suit has ceased to have his right treat it as rent suit under the Bengal Tenancy Act. 

 6. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, learned Counsel appearing for the respondent finds it difficult to assail the judgment of the Court of appeal below, as there is a concurrent finding of the Courts below that the judgment-debtor himself filed an application under Order 21, rule 90 and the execution proceeding was taken under Order 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The finding of the learned Subordinate Judge resign that of the trial Court is that the process were deemed to have been served on the judgment-debtor is not in possession of the disputed land. In the face of this finding which is a finding of fact the contention that the unction sale took place in rent execution case, cannot be accepted. Moreover, there is a clear finding by the Court of appeal below that the proceeding was not taken under the Bengal Tenancy Act, but under the Civil Procedure Code and it is to be held that it was disposed of as a money decree and as such there was no scope for interferon with the order of the Court of appeal below by the High Court Division.
